node.name: Flow Pace
node.notes: Pacing for Google Flow: one image request every ~8s plus generation time, so the account never sees a burst. Under 65s so the execution stays in memory and the static-data counters survive.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ sceneId: $json.sceneId, field: "image", url: $json.url, fields: { "Image Media ID": $json.mediaId, "Aprobare Imagine": false, "Regenerează Imagine": false, "Status Producție Scenă": "Așteaptă Aprobare Imagine" } }) }}

node.name: Wait IMG Cooldown
node.notes: 60s ON PURPOSE: under 65s the execution stays in memory and the cooldown counter in static data survives.

node.name: User Ref?
node.notes: The producer's reference photo (Editing Options.refImage, a Drive URL) has to be a Flow media id to serve as a reference. Upload it once and remember the id as refImageMediaId; later passes and restarts skip this.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { try { const o = JSON.parse((($json.fields || {})['Editing Options']) || '{}') || {}; return !!(o.refImage && String(o.refImage).startsWith('http') && !o.refImageMediaId); } catch (e) { return false; } })() }}

node.name: Save User Ref Id
node.notes: A jsonb merge, not a read-modify-write of the whole Editing Options: the site merges the same way, so a concurrent write from the project page cannot be lost.

parameters.query:
update hov.project
   set editing_options = coalesce(editing_options, '{}'::jsonb) || $hov${{ JSON.stringify({ refImageMediaId: $json.mediaId }) }}$hov$::jsonb
 where id = $hov${{ $('Receive Batch Input').first().json.Project_ID }}$hov$
returning id, editing_options->>'refImageMediaId' as media_id
